To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have proposed an evolutionary computing model for within-host dynamics that simulates two intruders detection paradigms in which the intruders are represented as an evolving guest (e.g. virus, computer program, etc.) infecting a host (e. g. mouse, computer memory, etc.).
the proposed WHD evolutionary computing model simulates the coexistence of two evolutionary systems in which one of the systems is an invader and the other system is a host.

the evolutionary computing model proposed here successfully simulates two detection paradigms of an intruder (humoral, danger), and that it can be applied to a wide range of problems in which the invader is evolving.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of evolutionary computing techniques for the study of within-host dynamics.
the study of the evolution of a guest within a host.
the evolutionary study of within-host dynamics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the model proposed in this work is a useful and effective tool in the study of within-host dynamics, which can be used in a wide range of applications.
the proposed WHD evolutionary model is an alternative to the traditional ODE model, and is useful for the design of anti-intruder systems.
this study is an initial step towards the development of a novel evolutionary WHD model.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have successfully proposed and simulated a model for the study of the coevolution of two entities, an invader (e.g., a virus, computer program) and a host (e..g., mouse, computer) in which the former can evolve within the latter.

we developed a model that simulates the evolutionary dynamics of a guest inside a host, where the guest and the host are modeled by an artificial immune system (AIS) and a genetic algorithm (GA), respectively.
the proposed model may be useful for the study of within-host dynamics in which the invader exhibits evolution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in the future, we will be able to simulate the evolution of an invader (e.g., computer virus) within a host (e-mail, computer, etc.) using an evolutionary computing model.
the proposed evolutionary WHD model can be used as a general tool for the study of within-host dynamics in which the intruding entity exhibits evolutionary changes.
the proposed model can simulate the coexistence of two entities that evolve within the same environment.
